decisions.statement: A caller in node pays bun's startup for each command asked as a child.
Bun's startup is about a fifth of a second.
A command's own work is measured in milliseconds.
This server is spawned as a program rather than imported.
The help names the file running rather than a path spelled here.
An ask arrives on stdin.
An answer goes out on fd 3.
A command writes the command's own answer to stdout.
The protocol therefore has a stream of the protocol's own.
A byte escaping onto stdout is the caller's to log rather than an answer.
The first line on fd 3 is hello.
Nothing is asked before hello.
An ask names a module under `module:` and an export under `export:`.
An ask read as a type keeps the wire's words rather than the words inside.
The client declares both wire keys.
Nothing is remembered between one ask and the next.
An ask re-runs a command against the files as the files are when asked.
A run is wrapped in one call.
The per-call memos are therefore as new as the memos in a child just started.
A held-open runtime cannot make fresh the code the runtime loaded.
This server therefore refuses to live.
A server past a lease answers nothing and exits.
A server finishing stays for the goodbye.
A caller reads an exit before a pipe where the two arrive together.
A lease is spent on the next ask rather than by a clock killing the process.
The ask spending a lease is refused by name.
A caller reading a lease refusal starts another server.
A caller waiting past the idle bound reads a server as gone rather than as late.
The one path a lease turnover takes is therefore the one path a test walks.
An answer has the age of the server composing the answer.
An answer has the pid composing the answer.
An idle bound reaps a server whose caller stopped asking without closing stdin.
An idle bound is above the lease.
An idle bound below the lease would reap a server before a lease turned over.
The server runs commands in series.
Capturing stdout means replacing stdout for the length of a run.
A command is loaded when first asked for rather than at startup.
A command whose imports throw refuses only the asks for that command.
An export answers through stdout.
The bytes an export wrote on stdout are the answer.
An export takes the arguments and the call.
An export answers a report and a code.
The file an export sits in is the code beside the page the ask names.
That page is looked for among the modules and then among the commands.
The page answering is the first of those whose code holds the export asked for.
A module sharing a slug with a command shadows it only where it answers.
The page is answered from the index rather than assembled from a name.
The index read is the checkout this server's own file sits in.
The repository a call works on is the repository the environment names.
A run is given the path of the file the export sits in as `argv[1]`.
An answer is said the way a command says an answer.
The caller's short-read guard therefore keeps working.
The protocol the caller reads has no reach into `Bun`.
The editor's node host imports the protocol the caller reads.
A slug no page carries is refused as unserved.
A slug no page of either type exports that name from is refused as unserved.
That refusal names every file read looking for the export.
No caller of this server spawns a child of its own.
A partial write is ordinary on a pipe rather than a fault.
Saying a line means saying the whole line.
The server's own voice is fd 2 written straight.
A run has replaced `process.stderr.write` for as long as the run lasts.
A server exits when stdin closes.
Stdin closes when the caller dies.
A command that throws while running is refused by name rather than answered.
A throw anywhere in serving an ask refuses that ask and leaves the server up.
A rejection nothing catches ends the runtime.
An answer says the server ran the export whatever code that export answered.
A command refusing the ask answers a nonzero code rather than a refusal.
A refusal is the server's own.
Nothing a command decided is said as a refusal.
A lease once spent stays spent for every ask that follows.
An idle bound counts from the last answer rather than from the last ask.

definition: one bun runtime held open, answering commands over a pipe against no startup cost
